speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are here regarding acute diarrhea; to help me determine the cause, how many times have you had unformed stools in the last 24 hours?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection (C. diff). Given your recent treatment with levofloxacin for pneumonia and the onset of frequent watery diarrhea with cramping, these findings are highly suggestive of antibiotic-associated colitis. I need to confirm if you have experienced fever, blood in your stool, or severe pain before we proceed with testing.
